bill.title: A resolution condemning the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation and officials of the Government of the Russian Federation for committing crimes against humanity and war crimes in Ukraine.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations. (text: CR S1584)
bill.officialSummary: This resolution condemns the war crimes and crimes against humanity committed by the Russian government and Russian Armed Forces in Ukraine.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution formally condemns the Russian government and Russian Armed Forces for war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Ukraine. As a Senate resolution, it expresses the official position of the Senate but does not create new law, impose sanctions, or change U.S. policy. It is a symbolic statement of condemnation.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would condemn the war crimes and crimes against humanity committed by the Russian government and Russian Armed Forces in Ukraine.
plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what the United States does abroad. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation.
